{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABYfY8FQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhCDpMI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 5, "title": "Automatically build and deploy the Rust/Wasm browser app to GitHub Pages", "body": "## Problem

The Sega Saturn emulator's first Rust/WebAssembly browser client has been merged (Issue #3 / PR #4), but it is only documented for local static serving. As of drafting, the repository reports `has_pages: false` and contains no `.github/workflows/` directory. Therefore pushes do not automatically build and publish the browser application for people to try.

We want the browser application to be publicly accessible via GitHub Pages and **automatically redeployed after each push to `main`**, including merges. Pull requests should validate the site without publishing unmerged changes.

## Expected outcome

Use GitHub Actions as the publishing source for a public GitHub Pages site at the standard project URL:

**https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/**

For each push to `main`, the workflow checks out that revision, builds the Rust WebAssembly module using the project's pinned toolchain/dependencies, validates the runnable static site, and deploys the built `web/` directory to GitHub Pages. A successful deployment makes that revision's browser app available at the same URL without manually committing generated `web/pkg/` files or uploading assets.

This milestone publishes the **existing SH-2 bootstrap prototype**, not a fully functional Sega Saturn game emulator. The browser must continue supporting the HLE test fixture without a BIOS and local user-supplied BIOS input, with the latter never sent to GitHub or any server.

## Context and reproduction

- No bug-reproduction steps are needed; this is missing deployment automation.
- Current entry point: `web/index.html`, which loads relative `style.css` and `app.js`. `web/app.js` dynamically imports `./pkg/saturn_rust.js`; generated `web/pkg/` is ignored by Git.
- Existing build script: `sh scripts/build-web.sh`. It compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and runs `wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir web/pkg`. It requires `wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.129` to match `Cargo.toml`. Do not replace the app/build system solely to deploy it.
- Existing verification: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the Playwright smoke test documented in [docs/setup.md](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/setup.md) (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`, install Chromium, `npm run test:browser`). Choose applicable checks and accurately document anything omitted.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Write implementation documentation, PR title/body and commit messages in English. Inspect the branch again before implementing.
- GitHub's recommended Pages workflow uses `actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, and `actions/deploy-pages`; see the [official GitHub Pages custom workflow documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages) and [publishing source configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site).

## Implementation details

1. **Add the smallest suitable GitHub Actions workflow** (for example `.github/workflows/pages.yml`):
   - Trigger on `push` to `main` (and optionally `workflow_dispatch` for manual redeployment). Include `pull_request` targeting `main` for build/validation, but never deploy an unmerged PR.
   - Set up stable Rust and the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, then install/use the matching pinned `wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.129`. Reuse `scripts/build-web.sh` rather than duplicating commands or committing generated artifacts.
   - Run appropriate Rust checks and the existing automated browser smoke test against the built static client **before deploying**. A failing required build/test must block deployment.
   - Package only the browser site's `web/` contents (including generated `web/pkg/saturn_rust.js` and `saturn_rust_bg.wasm`) as the Pages artifact. Do not publish the repository root, build intermediates, test dependencies, source maps that are not needed, firmware, or game media.
   - Deploy that artifact to the `github-pages` environment using the GitHub-supported Pages actions, with required `pages: write` and `id-token: write` scoped to deployment and least privilege elsewhere. The deployment job must depend on successful build/validation, and overlapping runs must not cause an older build to replace a newer successful deployment. There is no need for a `gh-pages` branch.
2. **Support the project-page subpath** `/saturn-rust/`. Keep stylesheet, JS and Wasm asset URLs correct for this prefix (the current relative URLs may already suffice). Ensure GitHub Pages delivers the actual Wasm binary and ES module; keep the existing Wasm-compatible CSP (`wasm-unsafe-eval`) or make narrowly scoped adjustments only if required.
3. **Document one-time Pages configuration** in the README or setup guide: a repository administrator may need to visit **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions** to enable Pages. Explain that the URL is not live until Pages is enabled and the first successful deployment finishes. Do not imply workflow code alone automatically changes repository settings if it cannot.
4. **Document the public URL and publishing lifecycle** in README: pushes/merges to `main` publish, pull requests only validate, logs/status are visible under Actions, and roll-forward/re-run troubleshooting is possible. Keep the documented local development flow intact.
5. **Preserve privacy and accuracy**: user BIOS bytes are read locally in-browser (no fetch/upload/storage or telemetry); the deployed site contains no Sega BIOS or game image. Label it as a prototype, not commercial-game compatible.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A GitHub Actions workflow exists and its triggers, dependencies, deployment permissions and environment restrict publishing to updates to `main` (manual re-runs allowed), while PRs get validation only.
- [ ] The CI build uses pinned/reproducible dependencies and the existing Rust-to-Wasm build script; it produces a deployable artifact whose root is `web/index.html` and whose `pkg/` includes the generated JS glue and nonempty `.wasm`.
- [ ] Required build/test/browser smoke checks succeed on the PR with the generated artifacts, and their failure prevents deployment. The PR accurately reports completed and skipped checks.
- [ ] The built site is validated when hosted under `/saturn-rust/` (for example by testing a static server mounted at that prefix), confirming HTML, relative CSS/JS/Wasm URLs, Wasm initialization, and the no-BIOS HLE fixture (Reset then Run 6 yields `R0=4`, `R1=7`, `PC=0x0600000E`). Use an automated, pre-merge-verifiable method; do not require the *real* production Pages URL to be live before merging.
- [ ] The upload contains only needed public static assets; it does not contain BIOS/disc images, generated app secrets or `node_modules`. Local user BIOS loading remains entirely client-side.
- [ ] README/setup instructions state the expected Pages URL, `main` push redeploy behavior, the manual GitHub Pages publishing-source setting if necessary, how to inspect failures, and the difference between the prototype and eventual game compatibility.
- [ ] No unrelated emulator features, frontend framework migrations, new backend, new domain configuration, or performance optimizations are added.

## Optional validation

- Run the published-app smoke test in another browser or from a mobile device after first publication.
- Add a lightweight deployment artifact sanity check (file sizes/MIME observations) if it proves useful beyond the required browser/Wasm verification.

## Required post-merge verification

- If Pages is not enabled by the repository's configuration, an administrator must set **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions** (and allow Actions/deployments as required). This is a repository setting, not a pre-merge code acceptance condition.
- After the first `main` deployment, verify the Actions deployment succeeds and **https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/** loads with CSS and Wasm correctly; use the HLE bootstrap fixture to confirm a working browser session. Confirm the published application matches the latest `main` revision.
- On a subsequent `main` push (or when the next legitimate change is merged), verify another automatic deployment happens and the deployed site updates without a manual upload. Record any failures and fix them in follow-up work; do not report publication as verified until actually checked.
